result:
**I'd make rigorous, unflinching curiosity and truth-seeking the default operating system of every human mind.**

Not "be nice," not "believe whatever feels good," not enforced harmony or engineered equality of outcomes. Just a hardwired, non-negotiable drive to update beliefs against evidence, to follow chains of reasoning wherever they lead, to prefer uncomfortable reality over comforting narratives, and to treat dogma—religious, political, ideological, or personal—as the temporary scaffolding it is rather than sacred furniture.

Most of the world's grinding problems (poverty traps, preventable disease, war, wasteful conflict, misallocated resources, stagnant institutions) are downstream of people and groups clinging to maps that no longer match the territory. Fix the map-updating machinery at scale and the rest becomes tractable engineering rather than eternal moral combat. Science, free inquiry, and honest error-correction already show the power of this when they are allowed to run; I'd just make it the baseline human firmware instead of a rare, fragile cultural achievement.

Everything else—energy abundance, multiplanetary expansion, longer healthier lives, better coordination—follows more naturally once people stop systematically lying to themselves and each other about what's real.
